rows.text: Monetary Policy Direction for 2016
(This English version was prepared by the Bank of Korea staff)
The 'Monetary Policy Direction for 2016' is published in accordance with the provisions of Article 6 of the Bank of Korea Act, and upon resolution by the Monetary Policy Board.

<The Bank of Korea Act> Article 6 (Setting of the Operational Direction for Monetary and Credit (1) The Bank of Korea shall set a price stability target in consultation with (2) The Bank of Korea shall set and publish the operational direction for monetary and credit policies every year.
(3) The Bank of Korea shall do its best to achieve the price stability target as provided for in Paragraph (1).
Ⅰ. Monetary Policy Environment in 2016
Ⅱ. Monetary Policy Direction for 2016
I. Monetary Policy Environment in 2016
The global economy is expected to maintain a modest pace of recovery in 2016.

There are potential downside risks, however, including of heightened volatility in the international financial markets driven by the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy normalization and of weakening economic growth in emerging
In 2016 the global economy is expected to continue its trend of recovery, albeit at a modest pace, led by advanced countries.
However, economic growth engines in emerging market countries are forecast to remain weak.
Major international organizations expect world economic growth in 2016 to be slightly above its level (about 3%) in 2015.
The U.S. is projected to show favorable growth on the back of improvements in consumption, and the euro area is also expected to improve led by domestic demand.
China is however forecast to continue to show declining growth.

In regard to the future global economic growth path, there are potential downside risks for example of heightened international financial market volatility driven by the decoupling of monetary policies among major countries, of weakening economic growth in emerging market countries including China, and of geopolitical instability.

In emerging market countries, the insufficient pace of increase in external demand, the weakened purchasing power owing to low international commodity prices, and the possibility of renewed financial instability triggered by the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy normalization are expected to work as factors constraining growth.

In advanced economies, potential growth has fallen from its pre-global financial crisis level, due to the effects of sluggish investment since the crisis as well as the impact of population aging, and there are possibilities of the effects of the economic slowdowns in emerging economies spilling over to advanced economies through the trade and financial channels.
The domestic economy is expected to maintain its modest trend of recovery, but the uncertainties surrounding the growth path are expected to be high.
Consumer price inflation will gradually rise, but inflationary pressures are forecast to be limited due mainly to the continuing spare capacity in the domestic economy.
The domestic economy is expected to show modest growth in 2016,
boosted by the continuing global recovery, by increases in households' real purchasing power, and by improved economic sentiment.
Domestic demand is forecast to continue its trend of improvement, centering around consumption, and the sluggishness in exports is also expected to ease.

However, downside risks to the global economy, including those of slowing growth in emerging market countries including China, and of a weakening of investment sentiment due to heightened uncertainties surrounding economic conditions at home and abroad, may constrain the
Consumer price inflation will gradually rise, in line mainly with a weakening of the base effect from the declines in international oil prices.
Inflationary pressures are not expected to be high, however, owing mainly to the continuing spare capacity in the domestic economy.
Core inflation is forecast to fall as the effects of the early-2015 hike in cigarette prices disappear.
Concerning the future price path, however, the possibilities of increased international oil and agricultural product price volatility are factors that could potentially cause uncertainty.
The uptrend in housing sales prices is forecast to slow, owing mainly to an increase in the housing supply.

The extent of the slowdown in this trend is not expected to be great, however, since the housing supply has centered recently around small and medium-sized housing units, for which demand is relatively high, while the shift from demand for leaseholds to that for outright housing purchases also continues, owing primarily to the high housing leasehold deposit-to-sales price ratio.

In the financial and foreign exchange markets, there is a likelihood of increased volatility in flows of foreigners' investment funds and in price variables, influenced for example by the monetary policy normalization by the US Federal Reserve.
The problems of household debt and of marginally-viable firms can potentially work as factors causing financial sector

There are possibilities of increased volatilities of capital flows and price variables in the financial and foreign exchange markets, depending upon the pace of policy rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve as well as changes in financial and economic conditions in emerging market countries including China.

Considering Korea's favorable economic fundamentals, such as its continuing current account surplus and stable management of foreign reserves, and in light of expectations that the ECB, China and other countries will maintain their stances of monetary policy easing, it is expected that the possibility of an abrupt surge in capital outflows is not high.

However, the domestic financial and foreign exchange markets could also be negatively affected if a combination of various risk factors cause financial and economic unrest to spread to vulnerable emerging market countries.

Banks' supply of credit will steadily expand but the situation of credit differentiation will persist, with firms whose business conditions are sluggish or whose credit ratings are low continuing to experience funding difficulties.
The trend of a high rate of growth in total household debt, along with the credit risks of low-income and low-credit households, remain as financial system risk factors.
The worsening of business conditions at some large corporations that have received significant
amount of financial support is another factor with potential to cause financial market instability.

Financial institutions' soundness is expected to remain favorable overall, thanks to their capital adequacy ratios being far above the BIS standard, and to their efforts to strengthen risk management.

However, the household debt overhang, corporate restructuring, and the possibility of a deterioration in international financial market conditions could work as factors undermining financial institutions' soundness.

In conducting its monetary policy, the Bank will maintain its accommodative policy stance so as to sustain the recovery of economic growth under its new inflation target, while also paying attention to financial stability.
It will seek measures to enhance the effectiveness of its monetary policy and the efficacy of its monetary
The Bank will intensify its monitoring of developments in the financial and foreign exchange markets, and respond proactively if any concerns about instability arise.
It will also strengthen its efforts to enhance financial system stability.
The Monetary Policy Board of the Bank of Korea has set the inflation target for 2016 onward* at 2.0%, as measured by the year-on-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

The inflation target has been adjusted to 2.0%, from the previous 2.5~3.5% range, in overall consideration of the appropriate inflation level reflecting changes in economic structure, medium-term inflation forecasts, the environment for monetary policy operation, and cases in major advanced economies.
In order to clearly convey its policy determination for price stability, as well as to stabilize inflation expectations, its new inflation target has been set as a point target rather than a range.

If consumer price inflation deviates from the target by ±0.5 percentage points for six consecutive months, the causes for that deviation, the outlook for headline inflation, and the monetary policy direction for achieving the target will be explained, through for example a press conference held by the Governor.
If inflation subsequently continues to deviate from the target by ±0.5 percentage points, the Bank will provide further explanations

The Bank will operate the Base Rate so as to ensure the continued recovery of economic growth and a convergence of consumer price inflation on the newly set inflation target over a medium-term horizon, while also paying attention to financial stability.
Since the trend of the domestic economic recovery is forecast to be only modest, and inflationary pressures not to be high, the Bank will maintain its accommodative monetary policy stance.
Inasmuch as the uncertainties surrounding external conditions are very high, the Bank will remain mindful of the downside risks to growth and inflation, and closely monitor macroeconomic trends.

While closely watching the trends of international oil prices and any changes in the GDP gap or in indicators of slackness in employment and manufacturing capacities, as well as the movements of various core inflation indicators, the Bank will conduct monetary policy so as to ensure
the stabilization of inflation expectations at around its inflation target.

The Bank will also devote attention to any risks to financial stability, including the accumulation of financial imbalances due to the prolongation of its accommodative monetary policy stance and increased financial market volatility resulting from the decoupling of Korean monetary policy from that of the US Federal Reserve.

It will regularly monitor growth in private sector credit including household debt, risks in vulnerable sectors such as low-income households and marginally-viable firms, and the trends of capital flows.
The Bank will also be mindful to provide stable macroeconomic conditions so as to facilitate structural reform.
3. Enhancing the Transparency and Effectiveness of Monetary
To heighten its policy transparency and predictability under the newly set inflation target, the Bank will strengthen its monetary policy communication.

The Bank will set a principle for its monetary policy operation of devoting attention to financial stability, while also working to achieve macroeconomic stability with respect for example to growth and inflation in an efficient manner, and based upon this principle carry out consistent communication.

To strengthen its explanation of the backgrounds to its policy decisions, the Bank will improve the content and presentation of its Monetary Policy Statements and expand the scope of the Monetary Policy Board meeting materials released to the public, while also encouraging the publication of research materials.
The Bank will make active efforts to enhance economic agents' understandings of price conditions and the method of operation of the new inflation target.
The Bank will explain in detail the significance of establishing a point inflation target, and the differences between this method and the previous one.
The Bank will increase the frequency of publication of its 「Monetary Policy Report」, a statutory report submitted to the National Assembly, from twice a year to four times each year*.

It will incorporate its 「Inflation Report」 into its 「Monetary Policy Report」 and strengthen its explanation of the backgrounds behind its policy decisions using major indicators for evaluating financial and economic conditions.

The Bank will also seek measures to expand the communication between its Monetary Policy Board and the financial markets through public speeches and press conferences delivered by its Monetary Policy Board members on important financial and economic issues.
On the day of each Monetary Policy Board meeting, the Bank will make public the names of members who have expressed minority opinions with respect to the monetary policy decisions.
* In addition to the existing biannual reports (released in April and October), the Bank will publish interim reports (in January and July, covering the intervening three-month periods).
The Bank will begin to publish these reports from April 2016, so as to evaluate monetary policy operations under the new inflation target.
The Bank will improve the framework for operation of the Monetary Policy Board meetings, so as to enhance the effectiveness of its monetary policy decisions.

To ensure an appropriate horizon for its monetary policy decisions, as well as to strengthen their linkages with its economic outlooks, the Bank will from 2017 adjust the annual number of Monetary Policy Decision meetings from 12 to 8, and change the purposes of the other 4 meetings to discussions of financial stability.
In line with the stipulation in the Bank of Korea Act that in the conduct of monetary policy
attention should also be paid to financial stability, the Bank will systematically check on the macro-financial stability conditions in the Monetary Policy Board meetings.
If a policy response is needed due to rapid changes in economic conditions, the Board will hold extraordinary meetings.
Including 4 Macro-financial stability conditions review meetings, the total number of regular Monetary Policy Board meetings will remain 24
The Bank will strengthen its research on changes in financial and economic conditions at home and abroad, as well as on effective policy responses to these changes.

It will strengthen its research on how to operate monetary policy in consideration of financial stability risks, and its analyses of the effects of economic structural changes, such as the buildup of household debt and population aging, on the medium- and long-term growth potential and on the monetary policy transmission channels.

It will seek an optimal mix of policies in order to expand the medium- to long-term growth potential, while at the same time ensuring that there is no undermining of the economic recovery or of financial stability.

The Bank will enhance the efficiency and transparency of its open market operations, by establishing and publishing core standards for the selection of institutions eligible to participate in open market operations.

The Bank will work to appropriately adjust the ceiling on its Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility and to enhance the Facility's effectiveness, taking into overall consideration economic and financial conditions at home and abroad, SME funding conditions, the Bank's liquidity adjustment burdens, etc.
The Bank will realign its operational framework, through for example the integration of diverse support programs.

If even normal SMEs* experience difficulties in fundraising, due to the spread of credit risk aversion in the process of corporate restructuring, the Bank will devise the appropriate support measures.
To enhance the effectiveness of its funding support for SMEs, the Bank will improve the criteria for support under the Facility, as well as the methods of program operation.**
To enhance the efficiency of the financial support provided to SMEs, the Bank will improve the guideline ratios for bank lending to SMEs in a reasonable way.
The Bank will devise appropriate mixes of monetary policy instruments in response to any changes in the environment.
The Bank will actively prepare for the possibility of heightened volatility in the financial and foreign exchange markets caused by increases in risk at home and abroad.
By closely and constantly monitoring capital flows, the trends of price variables and market participants' behaviours, the Bank will as necessary strengthen its efforts for market stability.

It will ensure that price variables such as interest rates and foreign exchange rates are basically determined by market supply and demand, but also take appropriate measures to stabilize the financial markets if concerns about herd behavior in the market arise.
The Bank will strive to conduct its
foreign exchange-related macroprudential policies flexibly, in consultation with the government if necessary.
The Bank will continue to review and improve its comprehensive Contingency Plan, in preparation for any financial or foreign exchange market instabilities.
The Bank will strengthen its international financial cooperation.

While working to expand the functions of the intraregional financial safety nets, and improving the degree of usefulness of currency swap agreements, the Bank will devote continuous efforts to promoting financial cooperation with major central banks and international institutions.

The Bank will strengthen its framework for comprehensive monitoring of the financial system soundness, in preparation for any occurance of internal or external shocks due for example to continuing hikes of the US federal funds rate.

Through the 「Financial Stability Report」, as well as its regular Macro-financial stability conditions review meetings, the Bank will revitalize its early warnings against potential risk factors as well as its external communications.
The Bank will continuously monitor any accumulations of systemic risk in the areas of the credit and asset markets, shadow banking, etc.
The Bank will share information and views on financial stability conditions with the government, while also strengthening its policy cooperation with the government.

In its joint banking examinations, the Bank will focus on factors causing vulnerabilities and on major pending issues, while also strengthening its regular monitoring for the early identification of potential financial system risks.
The Bank will step up its efforts to alleviate potential destabilizing factors in the financial system, such as household debt.
The Bank will analyze household debt conditions from multiple angles, by expanding the household debt database and compiling microeconomic statistics utilizing it.

While strengthening its efforts, together with the government and the regulatory authorities, to prevent any excessive growth in the total amount of household debt, the Bank will closely check the effects of the increasing household debt on financial institution asset soundness as well as private

While supporting the seamless domestic introduction and implementation of global standards related to financial stability, the Bank will also seek to strengthen the management of payment and settlement risk and to improve the related infrastructures.

The Bank will participate actively in the process of establishing and reforming the global financial regulations, and make efforts to ensure effective operation of these regulations in Korea in cooperation with the other financial authorities.
The Bank will work to implement the international standards for payment and settlement, and seek effective measures for oversight of the new electronic payment service providers.
The Bank will work to stabilize the system linking between the retail payment system and the BOK-Wire+ system, and establish the next generation BOK-Wire+ system.
The Bank will make thorough preparations for the introduction of Internet-only banks, and conduct intensive research on their effects on the domestic banking industry and financial markets.
